{"notes": "VISIT 3 (left 5:30). I still don't know who placed what. Ratings rest on what I heard, the picture, and Omar's private update.

Picture: the whole chain is now dark and connected: start run, top body, tail loops, lower fin, belly (reaches the tail junction), and the upper fin (x24-30, y6-10). The notch looks closed. Pale leftovers are harmless since they aren't connected: a stray line near Jack's hands going up to about (22,4.5), and a pale curl inside the tail loop around (24-28.5, 10.5-12.5).

Sofia: Spoke at 4:30 and 4:45 with accurate status, offered to carry Omar's belly, chased Hana on the fin, and flagged the sharp lower-fin turn to Jack and later Omar. Strong on collaboration and informal leadership. Minor slip: at 4:30 she said Hana was fixing the fin, but it was still pale at 4:45. Rating high.

Omar: Delivered the belly (reached the junction at 5:00, which matches the picture) and told me privately and openly. Then took the initiative on the upper fin, saying at 5:15 that he was bridging it and would stay clear of Hana. That is a strong finish with clear communication. Possibly the best impact and execution on the team. He probably did the fin bridge, but I didn't see it, so I'm crediting the intent and not the placement.

Hana: Silent with me again this visit. Her promised fin check never visibly happened. Sofia and Omar both had to prompt her, and the fin was still pale at 5:15. I have no evidence she did the fix. Early planning was good, but impact and leadership are low-mid. Worth asking her directly in the review.

Jack: Silent again, with no replies to Sofia's prompts. His hands are at a stray pale line that isn't connected. No visible contribution to the final chain. Collaboration and impact are low. I'll ask him in the review what he built."}
